questions.problem:
The closed, positively oriented curve $C$ is defined as $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector on $C$ can be expressed as

$$
n=\frac{a(t)\,i+b(t)\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.
$$

Find the function $a(t).$
questions.worked_solution:
For convenience, we express $r(t)$ in column vector notation:

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the outward-pointing normal vector of a closed, positively oriented curve, we follow three steps:

**Step 1**: We compute the tangent vector ${r}^{′}(t).$

Differentiating the expression for $r(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Since $C$ is oriented counterclockwise, we rotate ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ *clockwise* to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Rotating the vector ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3**: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t)$ (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{1}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}[\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that $a(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$

questions.problem:
The closed curve $C$ is defined as $r(t)=6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector for $C$ can be expressed as

$$
n=\frac{a(t)\,i+b(t)\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.
$$

Find the function $b(t).$

*Hint: Observe that $C$ is traversed clockwise.*
questions.worked_solution:
For convenience, we express $r(t)$ in column vector notation:

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the outward-pointing normal vector of a closed, *negatively* oriented curve, we follow three steps:

**Step 1**: We compute the tangent vector ${r}^{′}(t).$

Differentiating the expression for $r(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Since $C$ is oriented clockwise, we rotate ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ *counterclockwise* to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise rotation is

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Rotating the vector ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3**: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t)$ (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{1}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}[\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=\frac{6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that $b(t)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$
